Trial 371 is a genuine measurement outlier (apparatus transient, observer error, or one-time environmental spike); remaining trials 372–376 are nominal and consistent with post-baseline baseline.

Trial 371 is the first sign of a genuine non-stationary process in pendulum_lab (slow drift, cyclic modulation, or threshold crossing); trials 372–376 are still consistent with noise atop underlying change, but baseline assumption (stationarity days 1–35) is invalid and requires investigation.

Trial 371 is a data-entry or transcription error: I misrecorded or misread the value; the true value is closer to 1.6540 (nominal), and the 1.6859 entry is a digit transposition, decimal-point error, or unit confusion.

Residual: a genuine physical cause I have not yet formulated (mechanical coupling between trial 371 and prior day-13 event; a rare apparatus state triggered by ambient conditions on day 35; or an error in my baseline calculation that makes trial 371 appear anomalous when it is nominal).

The perfect correlation (pendulum_lab ↔ resonator_obs, r=1.000) is a statistical artifact from multiple comparisons and small sample size (n=102); negative auto-correlations at 4–10 day lags are also noise; all four instruments are genuinely independent and stable within baseline assumptions.

The perfect correlation (pendulum_lab ↔ resonator_obs, r=1.000) is genuine but mediated by a shared environmental driver (e.g., settlement thermal cycle, vibrational mode, or power supply modulation) acting on the two instruments with a 3-day phase lag; negative auto-correlations hint at a 5–10 day cycle being aliased or damped.

My data recording or numerical pipeline has a systematic error: two of the four instrument readings are corrupted copies or scaled versions of others (explaining the perfect correlation and weak cross-checks); or my lag-search algorithm has a bug that creates false correlations.

All four instruments are real and independent, but I have not yet collected enough data (Day 40, ~350–460 trials per stream) to establish stable cross-instrument baselines; apparent correlations and lags will converge to zero or reveal genuine structure as n → 1000+.

Residual: a genuine instrumental or environmental pathology that I have not yet formulated, such as a mechanical coupling between apparatus components, a failure mode in my calibration procedure that varies by instrument, or a settlement-scale electromagnetic or vibrational transient on specific days that I have not yet correlated with my measurements.
